QuestionStmt.S: The dual of the converse of the inverse of the logical statement $p \to (q \to r)$ is equivalent to

Solution.S:
Step 1: Original statement is $p \to (q \to r)$.

Step 2: Inverse of $p \to (q \to r)$ is $\sim p \to \sim(q \to r)$.

Step 3: Converse of the inverse is $\sim(q \to r) \to \sim p$.

Step 4: Simplify the converse of the inverse.

$\sim(q \to r) \equiv q \land \sim r$.

So the statement becomes $(q \land \sim r) \to \sim p$.

This is equivalent to $\sim(q \land \sim r) \lor \sim p = (\sim q \lor r) \lor \sim p = \sim p \lor \sim q \lor r$.

Step 5: Find the dual of $\sim p \lor \sim q \lor r$.

The dual is obtained by replacing $\lor$ with $\land$ and $\land$ with $\lor$. Since we only have $\lor$, the dual is $\sim p \land \sim q \land r$.

Step 6: Express $\sim p \land \sim q \land r$ in the form of the options.

$\sim p \land \sim q \land r = \sim [p \lor q \lor \sim r]$.

Now $q \lor \sim r$ is equivalent to $r \to q$. So $\sim [p \lor (r \to q)]$.

Thus the dual is equivalent to $\sim [p \lor (r \to q)]$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\sim [p \lor (r \to q)]}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
